notes: Someone who gives testimony about what they have seen or heard. In Acts it is the disciples' job: "You will be witnesses to me" (1:8). The word later took on the sense of one who dies for the testimony, from which "martyr" comes.

range.note: One who dies for the testimony.

elsewhere.note: On the evidence of two or three witnesses.
You are witnesses of these things.
You made the good confession in the presence of many witnesses.
Jesus Christ the faithful witness.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Power, strength, or capability, from which we get "dynamite." In Acts it is the power of the Holy Spirit that makes the disciples witnesses (1:8), and the power by which signs are done (3:12, 4:7, 4:33).

elsewhere.note: You know neither the Scriptures nor the power of God.
The power of the Most High will overshadow you.
The gospel is the power of God for salvation.
To us who are being saved it is the power of God.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to devote oneself, to continue steadfastly
notes: To persist in something, to be constantly devoted to it. The believers "devoted themselves" to prayer (1:14) and to the apostles' teaching (2:42), and the apostles to "prayer and the ministry of the word" (6:4). The root means to hold firm.

elsewhere.note: He told his disciples to have a boat ready.
Be constant in prayer.
Ministers of God, attending to this very thing.
Continue steadfastly in prayer.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: The physical tongue, and by extension a language. At Pentecost the disciples speak in other "tongues" and the crowd hears "in our own language" (2:3-11). Paul later writes about speaking in tongues in worship (1 Corinthians 12 and 14).

elsewhere.note: They will speak in new tongues.
Various kinds of tongues.
Every tongue confesses.
Persons from every tribe and language.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Participation and sharing, partnership. The first believers were devoted to "the apostles' teaching and fellowship" (2:42), and the same word is used for sharing money (2 Corinthians 8:4, Romans 15:26). It comes from koinos, "common."

elsewhere.note: God called you into the fellowship of his Son.
They gave me and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship.
Your partnership in the gospel.
Our fellowship is with the Father and with his Son.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Someone who goes first and leads others: a founder, pioneer, or leader. Peter calls Jesus "the Prince of life" (3:15) and "a Prince and a Savior" (5:31). Hebrews uses it as "the founder and perfecter of our faith" (12:2).

elsewhere.note: The founder of their salvation.
The founder and perfecter of our faith.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to turn back, to turn around
notes: To turn around, to return. It is one of Acts' words for conversion: "Repent, and turn again" (3:19; also 9:35, 11:21, 14:15, 15:19). It pairs with metanoeō and means a change of direction.

elsewhere.note: Turn, and I would heal them.
He will turn many of the children of Israel to the Lord.
You turned to God from idols.
If anyone among you wanders from the truth and someone brings him back.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A name, and in the Bible the person's character, authority, and presence. In Acts, things are done "in the name of Jesus": the lame man is healed (3:6), salvation comes (4:12), and baptism happens (2:38). To act in someone's name was to act with their authority.

elsewhere.note: Baptizing them in the name of the Father.
Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.
The name that is above every name.
You who believe in the name of the Son of God.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Freedom of speech, frankness, and confidence in speaking. Acts uses it of the apostles speaking without fear before the council (4:13, 4:29, 4:31) and of Paul preaching (28:31). It is one of Luke's signature words for the church.

elsewhere.note: He said this plainly.
No one who wants to be known openly acts in secret.
That I may boldly make known the mystery of the gospel.
Let us then with confidence draw near to the throne of grace.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Rescue, safety, and salvation, from the same root as sōzō and sōtēr. Peter says "There is salvation in no one else" (4:12), in answer to a question about how a man was healed. It covers physical rescue as well as the fullest sense of salvation.

elsewhere.note: He has raised up a horn of salvation for us.
The power of God for salvation.
The gospel of your salvation.
How shall we escape if we neglect such a great salvation?

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: "With one mind," a favorite word of Luke's, used of the believers' unity in prayer and gathering (1:14, 2:46, 4:24, 5:12). In the New Testament it appears mostly in Acts, and once in Romans 15:6.

elsewhere.note: So that together you may with one voice glorify God.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Fear, and also reverence and awe. In Acts, "great fear" comes on those who hear of Ananias and Sapphira (5:5, 5:11), and the church walks "in the fear of the Lord" (9:31). It covers both terror and respect before God.

elsewhere.note: They departed with fear and great joy.
Fear fell upon him.
You did not receive a spirit of slavery to fall back into fear.
Knowing the fear of the Lord, we persuade others.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To obey someone in authority, from "to be persuaded" and "ruler." Peter says, "We must obey God rather than men" (5:29). It is also used of the sailors who did not heed Paul's advice (27:21) and in Titus 3:1.

elsewhere.note: Be submissive to rulers and authorities, to be obedient.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A Jew who spoke Greek and lived in a Greek-speaking culture, as opposed to the Hebrews who spoke Aramaic. The complaint in 6:1 is from the Hellenists. The word occurs only three times in the New Testament, all in Acts (6:1, 9:29, 11:20).

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To pelt with stones, to stone to death, the penalty for blasphemy under the law (Leviticus 24:16). It is used of Stephen's death (7:58-59), and of Paul at Lystra (14:19).

elsewhere.note: The tenants beat one, killed another, and stoned another.
Jerusalem, who stones those sent to her.
Jerusalem, who stones those sent to her.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Literally "hard in the neck," like an ox that won't take the yoke. It translates the Old Testament description of Israel as a stiff-necked people (Exodus 32:9). Stephen says it to the council (7:51). It occurs only here in the New Testament.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Breath, wind, or spirit. In Acts it is chiefly the Holy Spirit, who is promised in 1:5-8, poured out at Pentecost (2:4), and fills the church throughout.

range.note: The Holy Spirit, or a spirit being.
Life, the breath of a person.

elsewhere.note: The Holy Spirit will come on you.
Receive the Holy Spirit.
Those led by the Spirit of God are sons of God.
The Spirit searches everything.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Someone sent with authority. Acts 1:2 and 1:25-26 use it for the twelve, restored to its number with Matthias.

range.note: Someone sent to act with the sender's authority.
The twelve, and later others such as Paul.

elsewhere.note: Whom he also named apostles.
Paul, called to be an apostle.
An apostle not from men.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To dip or immerse. John baptized with water; Jesus' followers will be baptized with the Holy Spirit (1:5), and Peter calls for baptism "in the name of Jesus Christ" (2:38).

elsewhere.note: Jesus comes to John to be baptized.
Jesus is baptized in the Jordan.
Baptized into his death.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To change one's mind, to repent. Peter's call at Pentecost is "Repent, and be baptized" (2:38).

range.note: Regret and leave behind what was wrong.
A new direction for the whole life.

elsewhere.note: Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
Repent, and believe in the gospel.
Remember from where you have fallen, and repent.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Common, shared. The believers "had all things in common" (2:44, 4:32). The same word is used of what is ritually unclean, as in 10:14.

elsewhere.note: With hands that were defiled.
Nothing is unclean in itself.
A common faith.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: An assembly, a gathering of those called out. It is the word translated "church." Acts 5:11 is its first use in the book.

range.note: A city's gathering of free citizens.
God's gathered people in the Greek Old Testament.

elsewhere.note: I will build my church.
To the church of God that is in Corinth.
The church, which is his body.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Service, especially waiting on tables. The apostles say they should not give up the word of God to "serve tables" (6:2) and keep to "the ministry of the word" (6:4).

elsewhere.note: Martha was distracted with much serving.
Whoever has a gift of service.
The ministry of reconciliation.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To wait on someone, as at a table. The apostles say, "It is not right that we should give up preaching the word of God to serve tables" (6:2).

range.note: Serve in a role of care or leadership.

elsewhere.note: I am among you as one who serves.
Whoever serves me must follow me.
Let them serve as deacons.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A word, message, or account. In Acts the word grows: "The word of God spread" (6:7, 12:24, 19:20).

elsewhere.note: The seed is the word of God.
The word of God is living and active.
The Word of life.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To fall asleep, a gentle word for death. Stephen "fell asleep" as he died (7:60).

elsewhere.note: Many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep were raised.
Some have fallen asleep.
Those who are asleep.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: One who saves. Peter calls Jesus "a Prince and a Savior" (5:31).

range.note: A royal or divine title in the Greek world.

elsewhere.note: A Savior, who is Christ the Lord.
We eagerly await a Savior.
Our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Splendor, honor, and the visible presence of God. Stephen sees "the glory of God" (7:55), and begins by calling him "the God of glory" (7:2).

elsewhere.note: They saw his glory.
All have fallen short of the glory of God.
He is the radiance of God's glory.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To practice magic, to be a magician. Simon "had practiced magic" in Samaria and amazed the people (8:9). The word is related to the Magi (magoi) of Matthew 2. Acts also meets Elymas the magician (13:6-8) and the magic books of Ephesus (19:19).

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Literally "keeper of the bed," a man who served in a royal household, usually castrated; the word can also mean a high official. The Ethiopian was a treasurer of the queen (8:27-39). Deuteronomy 23:1 excluded eunuchs from the assembly, while Isaiah 56:3-5 promises them a place.

elsewhere.note: There are eunuchs who have been made eunuchs by men.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to guide, to lead along the way
notes: To lead along a road, to guide. The Ethiopian says, "How can I, unless someone explains it to me?" using this verb (8:31). It is the root of "hodegetics." Jesus uses it of the Spirit who will "guide you into all the truth" (John 16:13).

elsewhere.note: If a blind man guides a blind man.
Can a blind man guide a blind man?
He will guide you into all the truth.
The Lamb will guide them.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A road or way, and by extension a way of life. In Acts, "the Way" is the earliest name for the Christian movement (9:2, 19:9, 19:23, 22:4, 24:14, 24:22).

range.note: A way of life; the name for the early church.

elsewhere.note: The way is wide that leads to destruction.
Prepare the way of the Lord.
I am the way, and the truth, and the life.
The new and living way.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Holy, set apart for God. As a noun in the plural it means "the holy ones," the saints, Luke's and Paul's word for all believers. In Acts it first appears for believers in 9:13 (also 9:32, 9:41, 26:10). It is also the "Holy" in the Holy Spirit.

elsewhere.note: She was found to be with child from the Holy Spirit.
Called to be saints.
Sanctified in Christ Jesus, called to be saints.
The prayers of the saints.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A vessel, container, tool, or instrument. The Lord says Saul is "my chosen vessel" (9:15), to carry his name. Paul later says, "We have this treasure in jars of clay" (2 Corinthians 4:7), using the same word.

elsewhere.note: No one covers it with a jar.
Make one vessel for honorable use.
We have this treasure in jars of clay.
In a great house there are vessels of gold and silver.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To stand up, rise, and also to be raised from the dead. It is the verb of resurrection: Jesus "rose" (see Acts 2:24, 17:3), and Peter says to Aeneas and Tabitha, "Arise" (9:34, 9:40). The related noun is anastasis, "resurrection."

elsewhere.note: The men of Nineveh will rise up.
The girl got up and began walking.
On the third day rise.
Your brother will rise again.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To make clean, in the ritual or the moral sense. In the vision Peter hears, "What God has cleansed, don't you call unclean" (10:15, 11:9). The same word is used for cleansing lepers in the Gospels.

elsewhere.note: Be clean; his leprosy was cleansed.
I will; be clean.
Let us cleanse ourselves.
He will cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Literally "one who receives the face," someone who judges by outward appearance, rank, or nationality. Peter says, "God shows no partiality" (10:34). Related forms appear in Romans 2:11 and James 2:1-9.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A follower of Christ, formed like "Herodian" or "Caesarian" as a label for the party of a leader. It was first used at Antioch (11:26), probably by outsiders. It appears only three times in the New Testament: here, in 26:28 on Agrippa's lips, and in 1 Peter 4:16.

elsewhere.note: If anyone suffers as a Christian, let him not be ashamed.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to encourage, to exhort, to comfort
notes: To call alongside: to encourage, urge, comfort, or appeal. Barnabas "exhorted them all to continue with the Lord" (11:23); his name means "son of encouragement" (huios paraklēseōs, 4:36). It is the root of paraklētos, the Counselor.

elsewhere.note: They shall be comforted.
With many other exhortations.
The one who exhorts, in his exhortation.
Who comforts us in all our affliction.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: An elder, an older person, and in the church a leader chosen from among the mature members. The first elders appear in Jerusalem (11:30), and Paul and Barnabas appoint elders in each church (14:23). The related word "presbyter" gives "priest" and "Presbyterian."

elsewhere.note: He must suffer many things from the elders.
Let the elders who rule well be considered worthy of double honor.
Appoint elders in every town.
I exhort the elders among you.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A messenger, whether human or heavenly. In Acts, an angel appears to Philip (8:26), Cornelius (10:3), and Peter (12:7-11), and strikes Herod (12:23). The Greek word underlies "angel" and "evangelist."

elsewhere.note: An angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream.
The angel Gabriel was sent.
He made it known by sending his angel.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Prayer, and also a place of prayer. The church prayed constantly for Peter (12:5), and gathered in Mary's house to pray (12:12). Luke's Gospel and Acts are full of prayer, at key moments and before key decisions.

elsewhere.note: My house shall be called a house of prayer.
He spent the night in prayer to God.
Be constant in prayer.
In everything by prayer and supplication.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To mark off by a boundary, to set apart for a purpose. The Spirit says, "Separate Barnabas and Saul for me, for the work to which I have called them" (13:2). Paul uses it of himself, "set apart for the gospel" (Romans 1:1; Galatians 1:15).

elsewhere.note: He will separate them one from another.
Set apart for the gospel of God.
Who set me apart before I was born.
Be separate from them.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To serve publicly, to perform a service, especially priestly service in the temple, and in the church to serve the Lord in worship. The Antioch leaders were "serving the Lord" when the Spirit spoke (13:2). It gives us "liturgy."

elsewhere.note: They ought also to be of service to them in material blessings.
Every priest stands daily at his service.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To put in order, assign, appoint, or determine. "As many as were appointed to eternal life believed" (13:48). The sense of the passive form (tetagmenoi) has been argued: appointed, destined, or inclined. The word is used of authorities that are "appointed" in Romans 13:1.

elsewhere.note: To the mountain to which Jesus had directed them.
I am a man set under authority.
Those that exist have been appointed by God.
They have devoted themselves to the service of the saints.

uncertain: What "appointed to eternal life" means about God's choice and human response in Acts 13:48 is debated; the Greek word allows more than one reading.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To live, be alive. Paul calls God "the living God" (14:15), set against the dead idols of the Lystrans. It is a regular name for the true God throughout the Bible (Joshua 3:10, Matthew 16:16).

elsewhere.note: You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.
As the living Father sent me, and I live because of the Father.
The righteous shall live by faith.
Serve the living and true God.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To announce good news. In Acts the verb runs from Jerusalem to the ends of the earth: Philip preaches the good news to Samaria (8:4-40), Paul to Lystra (14:7).

elsewhere.note: The poor have good news preached to them.
How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news.
The good news was preached to us.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A change of mind that leads to a change of life. The Jerusalem church concludes that God "has also granted to the Gentiles repentance to life" (11:18).

elsewhere.note: Produce fruit worthy of repentance.
Repentance and remission of sins should be preached.
God's kindness leads you to repentance.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Release, forgiveness. Paul announces that "through this man is proclaimed to you remission of sins" (13:38).

elsewhere.note: The blood poured out for the forgiveness of sins.
Repentance and remission of sins.
Redemption, the forgiveness of sins.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Light. Paul and Barnabas quote Isaiah 49:6: "I have set you as a light for the Gentiles" (13:47).

elsewhere.note: You are the light of the world.
A light for revelation to the Gentiles.
God is light.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Pressure, distress, tribulation. "Through many afflictions we must enter into the Kingdom of God" (14:22).

elsewhere.note: Then there will be great tribulation.
In the world you have trouble.
Tribulation produces perseverance.

notes: A kingdom, a rule or reign. Acts begins with "the Kingdom of God" (1:3) and ends with it (28:31).

range.note: The right and power to rule.
The people or territory a king rules.
The age when God's will is done on earth as in heaven.

elsewhere.note: The kingdom of heaven is at hand.
The kingdom of God is at hand.
My kingdom is not of this world.
